review_method: AI visual inspection of 64 systematic frames and 24 additional temporal samples. Qualitative findings, not independently annotated ground truth or measured model accuracy.

recordings.label: Beijing 2022 · China–Canada
recordings.observed: Edited single-view broadcast: useful near-overhead house views, guard-area crops, player close-ups and oblique views. Digital score/end/stone overlay is present in the samples.
recordings.opportunity: Best geometric control example: some views expose rings, centre/tee lines and distinct red/yellow stones.
recordings.difficulty: Camera cuts and framing changes invalidate a single calibration. House crops do not establish full guard coverage. People can occlude stones.
recordings.completeness: Potentially useful board views, but no per-shot completeness established.
recordings.next: Use as an overhead baseline, not the sole customer acceptance example.
recordings.temporal: At 61:17, the 12-second probe changes from an overhead house view to player close-ups. A board-view detector must stop carrying the image calibration across that cut.

recordings.label: 2022 wheelchair mixed doubles · Canada–Latvia
recordings.observed: Two side-by-side oblique camera views with physical scoreboards. Only 480p offered in this metadata snapshot. Foreground players and wheelchairs overlap the house in several samples.
recordings.opportunity: Recurring panel geometry could support persistent per-camera calibration, if stability is verified over time.
recordings.difficulty: Small distant stones, strong perspective, occlusions and scoreboard legibility. The views cover different ends; do not merge them as if they show the same board simultaneously.
recordings.completeness: Some house layouts are visible; complete per-shot states and identities remain unverified.
recordings.next: Use as a low-resolution stress case after the 1080p split-view path works.
recordings.temporal: At 32:02, a stone travels through the left panel while the right panel contains the other end's house. This is direct evidence that a still image alone cannot label the whole recording as settled.

recordings.label: Edmonton 2022 · mixed-doubles minigames
recordings.observed: Two camera panels, each showing parts of adjacent sheets. Players and stored/grouped stones occur around the houses. The recording lasts over two hours despite the catalogue's 'MD 2-end' description.
recordings.opportunity: Repeated geometry and visible rink lines are suitable for testing camera/sheet registration.
recordings.difficulty: Panel identity is not sheet identity. One frame contains several houses; team/sheet routing is necessary before state assembly. Resolution is 480p.
recordings.completeness: No trustworthy automatic match or board completeness can be inferred from the catalogue row alone.
recordings.next: Treat as a multi-sheet training challenge. Do not use '2-end' as the recording duration or assume one game per file.

recordings.label: Edmonton 2022 · four-player training
recordings.observed: Two recurring oblique end views, a physical scoreboard, near-house wheelchair occlusions and groups of stones near the side/back area. The nearer view includes a foreground barrier.
recordings.opportunity: Stable-looking framing in the eight sampled images offers a useful calibration-persistence test.
recordings.difficulty: 480p, perspective and occlusion limit stone separation. Need to distinguish active stones from stones outside play and avoid inferring that all detected stones belong to the current board.
recordings.completeness: House visibility varies; continuous post-shot coverage not established.
recordings.next: Keep as a distinct training-footage test after competition footage.

recordings.label: Richmond 2022 · two simultaneous matches
recordings.observed: Split screen contains different sheets, with physical scoreboard sheet numbers 3 and 4 visible. The view within a panel changes between ends across sampled times. The catalogue associates two matches with this recording.
recordings.opportunity: Explicit sheet numbers can help establish routing and maintain match-specific timelines.
recordings.difficulty: A panel is not a permanently fixed camera; recalibration and end-direction tracking are needed. The rink logo interrupts ring appearance. Only 480p is offered.
recordings.completeness: Two match outputs may be needed from one video; target selection and mapping must be explicit.
recordings.next: Use as a multi-match/camera-switching stress case. Keep all rows for this video in one evaluation split.

recordings.label: Leduc 2022 · Frazier/Purvis–Joseph/Thiessen
recordings.observed: Two main oblique panels plus two small overhead house insets, physical scoreboard and sheet label. Highest available height is 1440; audit samples use 1080p AVC.
recordings.opportunity: Overhead insets may make house calibration easier than the main views. Wider main views can provide complementary guard context if associated correctly.
recordings.difficulty: Inset resolution is a fraction of the full frame. Insets crop guard areas and may be occluded. The same stone may appear in multiple views and must not be counted twice.
recordings.completeness: House geometry is promising; all-stone reconstruction still requires coverage and view-association checks.
recordings.next: Use as a second input family and test whether native 1440p improves small-inset position accuracy.
recordings.temporal: In the probe starting 62:52, people move while house stones appear stable in several samples. Stationarity checks should focus on stones/board regions, not require the whole image to be motionless.

recordings.label: 2024 wheelchair championship · Canada–Korea
recordings.observed: Two side-by-side end views at 1080p, physical scoreboard and substantial wheelchair/player occlusion. The sample at 108:15 exposes a relatively clear house in the right panel.
recordings.opportunity: A strong first customer-style development case: one catalogued match, recurring geometry and better resolution than the 2022 team recordings.
recordings.difficulty: Perspective is still strong and one house can be crowded while the other is clear. Need active-end selection, per-panel calibration and temporal occlusion handling.
recordings.completeness: Clearer candidate states exist; automatic reconstruction of every shot is not demonstrated.
recordings.next: Prioritise a full-video prototype on this source; use the broadcast as a control and other matches as later validation.

recordings.label: GSOC 2025 · four-panel recording
recordings.observed: Four camera panels cover two sheets/games. On-screen labels read 'CAN R v ITA' and 'CAN W v GBR', while the retrieved title and catalogue pair CAN Red with GBR and CAN White with ITA.
recordings.opportunity: Four views provide complementary end coverage once camera, sheet and team mappings are verified.
recordings.difficulty: Match-label conflict requires review rather than silently choosing one source. Each panel has only a fraction of the 720p canvas; wheelchairs, poles and rink-edge stones complicate detection.
recordings.completeness: Cannot assign validated team identities using the current metadata alone.
recordings.next: Quarantine the team mapping for review; retain raw observations. Use this as the explicit multi-match acceptance challenge.
recordings.temporal: The 12-second probe at 138:42 retains four panels while players move. The team-pairing discrepancy is visible in the persistent on-screen labels.
